purpose: Controlled native callback traces for moving-platform integration, MAP stop, and carry state.

static_callback.horizontal_integration: object+0x0A fixed-point velocity is added to x; MAP checks at 01F7:9E75/9EA6 stop, snap, and set object+0x54=0x46
static_callback.vertical_integration: object+0x0E fixed-point velocity is added to y; MAP checks at 01F7:9FB2/9FDF stop, snap, and set object+0x54=0x46
static_callback.direction_reversal: 01F7:9F35/9F4A and 01F7:A03D/A051 select +/-0x28000 and update direction bytes
static_callback.animation: 9DC7 never writes object+0x12 or an animation cursor; each initializer selects one static PLATFW slot (300 or 301), so the BOB record is a static platform frame rather than a callback animation table.
static_callback.player_overlap_shape: A075 tests object_x < player_x < object_x+object_width and object_y <= player_y < object_y+12; object_width is the live +0x3E geometry field (32 or 48 pixels by PLATFW variant), and accepted overlap publishes DS:5006=-1 for A0B2.

controlled_motion.interpretation: With the carry latch cleared, the original callback integrates the injected horizontal velocity; this is a controlled motion proof, not an unmodified level trajectory.

controlled_block.interpretation: The native MAP branch stops and snaps the platform at x=2112, zeros velocity, and counts down the 0x46 phase timer.

conclusions: Static and controlled native traces now establish fixed-point integration, MAP stop/snap, direction-selection branches, and player-carry helper reachability for the shared 9DC7 callback.
The injected-velocity traces intentionally do not claim the level's authored terminal/reset table or an original-runtime player-contact outcome; those remain separate open questions.
